questions.stem: A couple comes to you following the diagnosis of trisomy 21 in their 18-week fetus. They ask what medical problems may be anticipated for a child who has Down syndrome. Of the following, the medical problem that is encountered most frequently in infants who have trisomy 21 is:
questions.explanation: Down syndrome is characterized by several clinical features and associated anomalies. Among the neurological features, generalized hypotonia in the first two years of life is a key characteristic. While cardiac defects are common, affecting about 40% of cases, and duodenal atresia is also an associated anomaly, generalized hypotonia is a constant and prominent feature.

questions.stem: Which congenital heart defect is most frequently associated with Down syndrome?
questions.explanation: Ventricular septal defect (VSD) is the most common congenital heart defect in Down syndrome, followed by atrioventricular septal defects.

questions.stem: A 6-month-old infant with Down syndrome presents with hypotonia and poor feeding. Which of the following is the most common gastrointestinal anomaly in these infants?
questions.explanation: Duodenal atresia occurs in about 5% of infants with Down syndrome and is the most common gastrointestinal anomaly in this population.

questions.stem: At birth, a neonate with trisomy 21 is noted to have hypotonia, a flat occiput, and a single palmar crease. What is the initial recommended screening test for thyroid dysfunction in this infant?
questions.explanation: Newborns with Down syndrome are at high risk for congenital hypothyroidism. The initial screening recommended is measurement of TSH and free T4 in the neonatal period.
